content.title: Iowa vs. Illinois: What to know about the Hawkeyes' first Elite Eight game since 1987
content.text: Party like it's 1987.The Iowa Hawkeyes are back in the Elite Eight for the first time in nearly 40 years, when Dr. Tom Davis' team was led by Roy Marble, B.J. Armstrong, Kevin Gamble and Brad Lohaus. This time, it'll be first-year Hawkeyes head coach Ben McCollum patrolling the sidelines when Iowa takes on No. 3 seed Illinois for a chance to play in next week's Final Four.Here'st to know about the game.How to watch and stream Iowa vs. Illinois in the Elite EightWhen: 5:09 p.m. CT, Saturday, March 28Where: Toyota Center, HoustonTV channel: TBS/truTVLivestream: March Madness LiveNCAA Tournament tickets for Iowa vs. Illinois in the Elite Eight in HoustonTickets are available through Ticketmaster. With hometown team Houston eliminated in the Sweet 16 and a bevy of traveling Nebraska fans heading home, plenty of tickets have become available for Saturday's showdown. As of 11 a.m. Friday, tickets are available for as little as $40 per person.You can find tickets here.What to know about Illinois basketball: players to watch, numbers to knowIllinois earned a No. 3 seed with a 24-8 record on Selection Sunday, but the Illini play better than a No. 3 when they're at their best.Illinois is actually ranked N0. 4 overall on KenPom — two spots ahead of Florida, the South region's No. 1 seed Iowa already eliminated — and has the second-best offensive efficiency in the country.Freshman guard Keaton Wagler has been the star of the show for Illinois. Wagler arrived without the fanfare of a top recruit, but he has certainly played like one. He earned second-team All-America honors and enters the Elite Eight averaging 17.7 points, 5.1 rebounds and 4.3 assists per game.Fellow freshman David Mirkovic (13.7 points, 8.0 rebounds per game) has emerged as Illinois' No. 2 option. Mirkovic posted a 14-point, 10-rebound double-double in Illinois' Sweet 16 win over Houston and had a monster 29-point, 17-rebound effort in the first-round win over Penn.Illinois is an elite rebounding team (No. 3 in offensive rebounding percentage) and does not commit turnovers (ninth-lowest turnover rate). Defensively, they are dead last in all of Division I men's basketball in turnover rate, so Iowa shouldn't have too many turnover problems.Iowa vs. Illinois: series history, recap of their first meeting this seasonIllinois leads the all-time series 95-77 and is currently on a five-game winning streak against the Hawkeyes. The Illini have actually won 10 of the last 11 games in this series, with the lone Iowa win coming in February 2023 when Tony Perkins posted 32 points in an 81-79 victory at Carver-Hawkeye Arena.Illinois took a 75-69 victory at Carver on Jan. 11 in the only game played this season between these teams. Wagler led both teams with 19 points. Fellow Illini guards Kylan Boswell and Andrej Stojakovic each added 17. Bennett Stirtz had a tough shooting night, going 5-for-17 from the floor for 12 points. Tavion Banks saw success in this matchup the first time around, chipping in 16 points, 7 rebounds and 5 assists while shooting 57% from the field.Stirtz picked up his fourth foul with 11:36 to go in the second half of the first game between these two teams and only played 33 minutes as a result. He hasn't played fewer than 37 minutes in any game since, so it's safe to assume Iowa will have its star guard on the floor more this time around.» Subscribe to KCCI's YouTube page» Download the free KCCI app to get updates on the go: Apple | Google Play HOUSTON —Party like it's 1987.The Iowa Hawkeyes are back in the Elite Eight for the first time in nearly 40 years, when Dr. Tom Davis' team was led by Roy Marble, B.J.
